intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SEC61A1 gene (609213).

checks.claim: Common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SEC61A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found two heterozygous SEC61A1 mutations in patients of two unrelated families with an early-onset, infection-only antibody deficiency and normal (sub-)populations of peripheral B cells.
checks.explanation: The paper reports heterozygous SEC61A1 mutations (V85D and E381*) that segregate with primary antibody deficiency in two families. The discussion describes the phenotype as ranging 'from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID'. The 'CVID15' label is OMIM's name for this disorder, so its use restates the paper rather than adding a new claim.

paragraphs.text: Common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is an autosomal dominant primary antibody deficiency. Patients have low levels of IgM, IgG and IgA, or more broadly hypogammaglobulinemia, and recurrent bacterial infections of the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts. Peripheral B- and T-cell subpopulations are normal, but circulating plasmablasts are reduced and B cells do not differentiate normally into plasma cells. Severity varies, ranging from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID (Schubert et al., 2018).

checks.claim: CVID15 is an autosomal dominant primary antibody deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified a heterozygous missense mutation and a heterozygous nonsense mutation in SEC61A1.
checks.explanation: Paper reports heterozygous segregating mutations and dominant effects but never explicitly states 'autosomal dominant'.

checks.claim: Patients with CVID15 have low levels of IgM, IgG and IgA, or more broadly hypogammaglobulinemia.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe two families suffering from early-onset, severe, recurrent bacterial infections of the respiratory tract with antibody isotype deficiencies involving IgM, IgG and IgA.

checks.claim: Patients with CVID15 have recurrent bacterial infections of the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts.
checks.evidence_quote: suffered from severe recurrent bacterial infections such as tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections.
checks.explanation: The respiratory and gastrointestinal infections are described for Family I; the Family II index patient had no severe or recurrent infections on IVIG.

checks.evidence_quote: hypogammaglobulinemia, severe recurrent respiratory tract infections, and normal peripheral B- and T-cell subpopulations.

checks.evidence_quote: Only the very small population of peripheral CD27+CD38high plasmablasts appeared to be reduced in patients of Family I (Figure 2B). However, since this is a very small cell population
checks.explanation: Reduction shown only in Family I and the authors call this value error-prone.

checks.claim: In CVID15, B cells do not differentiate normally into plasma cells.
checks.evidence_quote: On in vitro stimulation, B cells showed an intrinsic deficiency to develop into PCs.

checks.evidence_quote: may be responsible for the fully penetrant PAD in Family I ranging from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID.
checks.explanation: The range is stated for Family I specifically, not for the disease overall.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied 10 affected individuals in a family with dominantly inherited antibody deficiency (Family I). They had isotype deficiencies of IgM, IgG and IgA. They had severe recurrent bacterial infections, including tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections, which in most cases began in the first year of life. The affected individuals did not respond to polysaccharide vaccination, and their responses to tetanus toxin vaccination varied. Their peripheral B-cell and T-cell subpopulations were normal, but they had fewer circulating plasmablasts, and their B cells showed defective plasma cell differentiation in vitro.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) also described a second family (Family II). The index patient (II.P3) was an 8-year-old boy who had had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth. Because he was treated with IVIG, he had not had any severe or recurrent infections. His B cells showed defective plasma cell differentiation in vitro, but his peripheral B-cell subpopulations were normal. His mother also carried the mutation but had a secondary immunodeficiency and was not included in the study. His grandmother (II.P1), another carrier, reported more frequent upper respiratory infections in childhood, with recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media. At age 66 her serum immunoglobulin levels were normal.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of CVID15 in the families reported by Schubert et al. (2018) was consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance. In Family I, the heterozygous mutation segregated with the disease in 10 affected individuals. In Family II, the mutation was passed from the grandmother through the mother to the index patient.

checks.evidence_quote: we confirmed that the heterozygous missense mutation (c.254T>A, p.V85D) in SEC61A1 perfectly segregated with the disease within Family I
checks.explanation: Heterozygous segregating mutations imply dominant inheritance, but the paper does not explicitly state autosomal dominant transmission.

checks.explanation: Segregation stated, but the number genotyped (10 affected) is not explicitly given in the text.

paragraphs.text: In the 10 affected members of Family I, Schubert et al. (2018) identified a heterozygous c.254T-A transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a val85-to-asp (V85D) substitution. Sanger sequencing confirmed that the mutation segregated perfectly with the disease in the family. In HeLa cells, the V85D mutation impaired cotranslational translocation of preprolactin. Overexpressing the mutant reduced the calcium load of the endoplasmic reticulum, which the authors attributed to a dominant effect of increased calcium leakage through the channel.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) carried out targeted sequencing of SEC61A1 in more than 200 additional patients with primary antibody deficiency and found a nonsense mutation in 1 of them. They identified a heterozygous c.1325G-T transversion in SEC61A1, resulting in a glu381-to-ter (E381X) substitution, in the index patient of Family II (II.P3). His mother and grandmother (II.P1) also carried the mutation. The gnomAD database listed no premature stop mutations in SEC61A1 in healthy individuals.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) suggested that in Family II, SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency caused hypogammaglobulinemia that was possibly transient, with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance. By contrast, they proposed that the dominant-negative V85D mutation may underlie the fully penetrant antibody deficiency in Family I, which ranged from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID.

paragraphs.text: Reimold et al. (2001) found that XBP1 transcripts were rapidly upregulated in vitro by stimuli that induce plasma cell differentiation. Introducing XBP1 into B-lineage cells initiated plasma cell differentiation. The authors concluded that XBP1 is selectively and specifically required for the terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes into plasma cells. Schubert et al. (2018) noted that SEC61A1 is a target gene of XBP1s. By proteomics, they found that SEC61A protein was about 2-fold more abundant in human peripheral blood plasmablasts than in naive and memory B cells.

checks.evidence_quote: XBP-1 transcripts were rapidly upregulated in vitro by stimuli that induce plasma-cell differentiation
checks.explanation: The abstract says this almost word for word.

checks.claim: Introducing XBP1 into B-lineage cells initiated plasma cell differentiation.

checks.evidence_quote: XBP-1 is the only transcription factor known to be selectively and specifically required for the terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes to plasma cells.
checks.explanation: The abstract's concluding sentence says this. The claim leaves out that the authors called XBP-1 the 'only' such transcription factor known, but what it does say is accurate.

checks.evidence_quote: SEC61A1 is a target gene of spliced X-box binding protein 1 and strongly induced during plasma cell (PC) differentiation.

checks.evidence_quote: the relative abundance of SEC61A protein is two-fold higher in plasmablasts from human peripheral blood as compared to naïve and memory B cells

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) found that purified B cells from mutation carriers in both families differentiated into plasmablasts and plasma cells significantly less well in vitro and secreted less IgG and IgA. EBV-transformed B-cell lines from patients lacked the CD38-high/CD138-positive plasma cell subpopulation and secreted less immunoglobulin. Naive B cells from carriers of the E381X mutation had reduced SEC61A1 protein, and no truncated protein was detected. The authors concluded that the nonsense mutation likely causes nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency. Stable expression of the V85D mutant caused GFP-positive cells to disappear from multiple myeloma cell lines but did not affect other cell lines. In myeloma cells, V85D activated the terminal unfolded protein response, with upregulation of PERK, ATF4 and CHOP.

checks.evidence_quote: We observed reduced expression levels of SEC61A1 in naïve B cells of II.P1 and II.P3

checks.evidence_quote: Using a second antibody recognizing the N-terminal domain of SEC61A1 in lysates from an EBV-transformed B cell line of II.P3, we excluded the presence of a shortened protein product
checks.explanation: Truncated protein was excluded in an EBV-transformed B-cell line from II.P3, not in naive B cells.

checks.evidence_quote: supporting the hypothesis that the nonsense mutation p.E381* likely results in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and leads to SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency in Family II.

checks.explanation: The gist is supported. The paper says 'upregulated' only for ATF4 and CHOP mRNA in L-363 cells; PERK (with ATF4) rose at the protein level ('significantly increased protein levels' in U266).

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied 10 affected members of a family (Family I) with IgM, IgG and IgA deficiency, severe recurrent bacterial infections and defective plasma cell differentiation (CVID15). In all of them they identified a heterozygous c.254T-A transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a val85-to-asp (V85D) substitution. The mutation segregated perfectly with the disease in the family, which showed linkage to chromosome 3 with a peak LOD score of 3.31. In HeLa cells, the mutant impaired cotranslational translocation of preprolactin and reduced the calcium load of the endoplasmic reticulum, consistent with a dominant effect from increased calcium leakage. In multiple myeloma cell lines, stable expression of V85D activated the terminal unfolded protein response.

paragraphs.text: In an 8-year-old boy (II.P3, Family II) with hypogammaglobulinemia since birth (CVID15), Schubert et al. (2018) identified a heterozygous c.1325G-T transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a glu381-to-ter (E381X) substitution. His mother and grandmother (II.P1) also carried the mutation. The grandmother had more frequent upper respiratory infections and recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media in childhood, but her immunoglobulin levels were normal at age 66. Naive B cells from carriers had reduced SEC61A1 protein, and no truncated protein was detected, which the authors took to indicate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and haploinsufficiency. B cells from carriers showed reduced plasma cell differentiation in vitro.
